titulo: The tag comes back to the counter
subtitulo: Check price and fit, ask the exchange rule before paying, then return with the receipt and tag
cena: The shirt fits perfectly under fitting-room light, and the only way to find out whether it survives the walk home is to actually wear it there.
frasePiso: You can turn a product you can see into a verified choice — price, fit, exchange condition and the right evidence for the return.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Mexican consumer protection distinguishes remedies for a defective or misrepresented product (repair, replacement or refund) from a size- or fit-based exchange, whose conditions are set by the individual store.
fatosDatados.fonte: Profeco — direitos básicos do consumidor; Profeco — garantia, reparação, reposição ou devolução

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Keeping the purchase receipt is recommended practice for any claim, exchange or return in Mexico, since it is the artifact stores and Profeco itself point to when resolving a case.
fatosDatados.fonte: Profeco — ticket/comprovante para reclamação, troca ou devolução

steps.pt: Recall B14's receipt — a shop receipt may need to travel back with the product. Ask for it again here.

steps.promptPt: Recall B14. The card payment is complete. Ask for the receipt. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
steps.pinyin: meh PWEH-deh dahr el reh-SEE-boh por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Can you give me the receipt, please?
At a shop, point before you name — esta camisa makes one visible item the question, price included.
How much does this shirt cost?

steps.promptPt: A shirt has no visible price. Point to it and ask the cost. Speak now.
steps.pt: How much does this shirt cost?
It costs six hundred pesos.
The frame is ¿tiene, plus the thing you want. The tag says your size; the garment is the evidence.
Do you have a larger size?

steps.promptPt: The shirt on the rack is tight across the shoulders. Ask for a larger size. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a larger size?
Yes, here you are.
Can I try it on?

steps.promptPt: The larger shirt is in your hand. Ask whether you can try it on. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I try it on?

steps.es: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.
steps.pt: Yes. The fitting rooms are at the back.
steps.tts: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.

steps.pt: Second shirt hangs loose — don't translate a size chart, just ask for the direction: una talla más chica.
Do you have a smaller size?

steps.promptPt: The shirt now hangs too loose. Ask for one size smaller. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a smaller size?
Yes, I'll bring you one.
Third size works — close it with me llevo esta: this one, not a catalogue of options.
I'll take this one.

steps.promptPt: This size fits and you want the shirt in your hand. Say you will take this one. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'll take this one.
Perfect.
Fit isn't a defect — don't assume the exchange rule. Before paying, ask if you can change it, and how many days you get.

steps.es: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?
steps.pinyin: lah PWEH-doh kahm-BYAHR see noh meh KEH-dah
steps.pt: Can I exchange it if it doesn't fit me?
steps.tts: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?

steps.promptPt: Before paying, ask whether the shirt can be exchanged later if the fit is wrong. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?
steps.pinyin: lah PWEH-doh kahm-BYAHR see noh meh KEH-dah
steps.pt: Can I exchange it if it doesn't fit me?

steps.es: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.
steps.pt: Yes, with the receipt and the tag.
steps.tts: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.

steps.pt: How many days do I have to exchange it?

steps.promptPt: The store accepts the exchange with receipt and tag, but you still need the deadline. Ask how many days you have. Speak now.
steps.pt: How many days do I have to exchange it?
You have thirty days.
Next morning, the fit is wrong under real movement. Tag attached, receipt in hand — ask for another size.
I want to exchange it for another size.

steps.promptPt: You return with the shirt. Ask to exchange it for another size. Speak now.
steps.pt: I want to exchange it for another size.
Do you have the receipt and the tag?
Yes, here they are.

steps.promptPt: The clerk asks for the receipt and tag. Put both on the counter and answer. Speak now.
steps.pt: Yes, here they are.

steps.promptPt: The fit is right but the colour is not. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have another colour?

steps.promptPt: The card machine is down. Offer the other way. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I pay in cash?

steps.es: ¿Cuánto cuesta esta camisa? ¿Me la puedo probar? ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda? Quiero cambiarla por otra talla.

steps.pt: B15 complete. Price visible, fit tested, sizes by direction, exchange policy asked before paying, receipt and tag kept.

aprofundar.titulo: Fit, policy and evidence are three different checks

secoes.titulo: The garment outranks the size label
secoes.corpo: Brand and market labels vary. Más grande and más chica describe the direction the fit needs to move without translating a sizing system.

secoes.titulo: A fit exchange is a question, not a promise
secoes.corpo: Legal protection for a defective or misrepresented product is not identical to changing a sound product because it does not fit. Ask the store's policy and deadline before paying.

secoes.titulo: Receipt and tag are portable evidence
secoes.corpo: The staff answer names the artifacts this particular store requires. Preserve both until the fit survives real use.
Esta camisa plants the object; me la puedo probar and cambiarla keep it alive. In a real shop, pointing is part of the sentence, not a failure.

permissao: You are allowed to ask the exchange question before you've even decided to buy the shirt. Asking about a policy you might never use is not presumptuous — it costs the clerk nothing to answer, and it costs you everything if you skip it and need it the next morning.
espelho: Anyone who has ever kept a receipt 'just in case' after an online order back home already understands B15's whole logic — asking the local exchange policy before paying is the in-person version of reading the returns page before you check out.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The shirt fit fine in the fitting room, but you get it back to the hotel and realise it's tighter than you thought, and you assume you're just stuck with it.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I already bought it, so there's nothing to be done, or asking to exchange it now would be pushing my luck.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A size- or fit-based exchange is a normal, store-specific policy in Mexico, distinct from the stronger legal protections for a genuinely defective product — most shops that sell clothing expect and accommodate this kind of return within a window, as long as the receipt and tag come back with the item.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Bring the receipt and the still-attached tag back to the same counter and ask to exchange for another size.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get the size that actually works, using exactly the artifacts the store already told you it needed.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not once you've removed the tag or missed the store's stated deadline — at that point the same policy that protected you no longer applies.

clique.desconto: Nobody gave you a separate sentence for clothes, for rooms and for medicine. One opening asked all three whether they had the thing you wanted.
clique.piso: Next time what's on the shelf isn't quite right, you won't settle for it. You'll ask what else they have.
